title: Continuous at room temperature
title_note: The paper's title is "Junction lasers which operate continuously at room temperature"; it makes no "first" claim. Temperatures are printed in °K and are heat-sink (copper block) temperatures, not junction temperatures (Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, p.110 col. 1). Parallel work: Alferov et al. (A. F. Ioffe Physicotechnical Institute) reported continuous room-temperature emission from small-area AlAs-GaAs heterojunction lasers, submitted 1970-05-06 (Fiz. Tekh. Poluprovodn. 4, 1826 (1970); Sov. Phys. Semicond. 4, 1573 (1971)); this letter was received 1970-06-08.
tagline: A four-layer GaAs-Al_{x}Ga_{1-x}As diode lases continuously on a diamond heat sink.

parts.name: fused silica tube
parts.role: Growth tube; hydrogen flows in at one end, out at the other.
parts.detail: Fig. 1 draws the graphite holders inside a fused silica tube in a furnace, with "H_{2} IN" at the push-rod end and "H_{2} OUT" at the stop end. The text says only that the layers were grown "in the apparatus shown in Fig. 1". Tube and furnace sizes, gas flow rate and furnace type are not given. The same group's patent describes the same kind of set-up for an earlier wafer: hydrogen passed through the tube, furnace at 870 °C (US 3,758,875 col. 8:52-56); those values belong to that run, not to this paper.
parts.quote: The layers were grown on polished and etched (111) and (100) faces of n-type GaAs in the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.
parts.locator: Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, p.109 col. 2; Fig. 1 (p.109)

geometry.gas: H2 in at right (push-rod end), out at left (stop end)

parts.name: single loop auxiliary heater
parts.role: Extra heater below the tube, under the growth region.
parts.detail: Labelled "SINGLE LOOP AUXILIARY HEATER" in Fig. 1, drawn as a coil running along under the tube, inside the furnace walls. Its power and purpose are not given in the paper. The patent's example describes "a single loop of about 2 feet of 20 mil nichrome wire heated by 20 volts a.c." disposed under the seed (US 3,758,875 col. 8:56-59, earlier run).
parts.locator: Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, Fig. 1 (p.109)

parts.name: thermocouple
parts.role: Reads the temperature just under the seed.
parts.detail: Fig. 1 draws the thermocouple entering from the stop end inside the sliding holder, its tip below the seed. The growth temperatures (layer 1 from 840 to 830 °C) are presumably read here; the paper does not say where they were measured.
parts.locator: Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, Fig. 1 (p.109)

parts.name: graphite seed holder
parts.role: Fixed graphite bar holding the seed; a stop at its end.
parts.detail: Fig. 1: a long hatched graphite bar with the seed set into its top surface near the stop end ("STOP", a round end piece). The sliding solution holder wraps around it and moves along it.
parts.locator: Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, Fig. 1 (p.109)

parts.name: graphite sliding solution holder
parts.role: Four wells of melt; pushed so each passes over the seed.
parts.detail: Fig. 1: a graphite block with four wells (solutions 1-4, left to right) between solid walls, sliding on the seed holder and pushed by a push rod from the far end. At the start a solid wall covers the seed; pushing the holder brings solutions 1, 2, 3 and 4 over the seed in turn. "After cooling rates of 1-3 °C/min had been established, the solutions were successively brought into contact with the seed." The patent example adds that the last close-fitting graphite surface wiped the residual melt from the seed (US 3,758,875 col. 9:6-9, earlier run).
parts.quote: After cooling rates of 1-3 °C/min had been established, the solutions were successively brought into contact with the seed.
parts.locator: Hayashi et al., Appl. Phys. Lett. 1970, p.109 col. 2; Fig. 1 (p.109)

parts.name: layer 2: GaAs (Si)
parts.role: Thin compensated p-type GaAs; the narrow active region.
parts.detail: Grown in 15 s from solution 2 (no Al). Thickness ≲ 1 µm in a typical run; target p ≈ (1-4)×10^{18} cm^{-3}, compensated. The authors credit the lower threshold "primarily" to a narrower active region than before and call a thin, uniform second layer "the most important factor"; the width was not yet optimized below 1 µm. In the Fig. 2 diode the emission was 80 meV above that expected for GaAs, attributed to a little Al carried over from solution 1.
parts.quote: The most important factor is that the second layer be thin and uniform although we have not, as yet, optimized the width at less than 1 µm.

parts.name: Fabry-Perot double-heterostructure diode
parts.role: Uncoated broad-area chip; the diode of Figs. 2 and 3.
parts.detail: The data of Figs. 2 and 3 are for "an uncoated Fabry-Perot double heterostructure diode 370 µm long and about 80 µm wide". The two end faces 370 µm apart form the resonator; they are uncoated. How the chip and its end faces were made is not stated (the patent's earlier diodes were "cut and cleaved", US 3,758,875 col. 9:47-48). No stripe contact is described. Other diodes: square, fully internally reflecting diodes reached J_{th}(300 K) as low as 1000 A/cm^{2} (text; the abstract prints 100 A/cm^{2}), and uncoated Fabry-Perot diodes 560 µm long about 1600 A/cm^{2}.
parts.quote: The data of Figs. 2 and 3 are for an uncoated Fabry-Perot double heterostructure diode 370 µm long and about 80 µm wide.

parts.name: light from the end faces
parts.role: Output through the two uncoated end faces.
parts.detail: Light leaves through the uncoated end faces of the Fabry-Perot diode. Lasing was recognized by the "turn on" of several spots seen with an image converter microscope, or spectrally (Fig. 3). At 297 K on its heat sink this diode gave at least 20 mW at 30 % above threshold (whether one or both faces were collected is not stated). The emission is near-infrared (about 1.45 eV in Fig. 3, about 0.86 µm, derived); the colour drawn is illustrative.

chapters.line: A polished n-type GaAs wafer waits in a graphite holder.
chapters.action: Fig. 1 section assembles (schematic): fused silica tube, auxiliary heater coil below, seed holder bar with stop, sliding solution holder with four filled wells, push rod, thermocouple under the seed. Hydrogen arrows run from the push-rod end to the stop end. A solid wall covers the seed. Furnace glow is ambient (temperature in the HUD only). Inset to the right: a small empty stack frame above the seed

chapters.line: The first melt slides over the seed; n-type Al_{x}Ga_{1-x}As grows.
chapters.action: push rod moves the holder toward the stop end until well 1 sits over the seed; HUD temperature counts 840 → 830 °C while the blue layer 1 rises on the seed in the inset (3-4 µm, drawn 3.5); holder moves on (a solid wall passes over the seed)

chapters.line: A brief touch of the second melt leaves a thin GaAs layer.
chapters.action: well 2 over the seed for a short dwell (HUD: 15 s, still cooling); the thin amber layer 2 appears on layer 1 in the inset; label shows the essential thickness

chapters.line: p-type Al_{x}Ga_{1-x}As closes the double heterostructure.
chapters.action: well 3 over the seed, 15 s; green layer 3 on layer 2 in the inset

chapters.line: A last GaAs layer for a better p-side contact.
chapters.action: well 4 over the seed, 15 s; violet layer 4 on top; then the last solid wall passes over the seed (the patent says it wipes the melt; the paper is silent, so no wiping detail). The apparatus fades; the inset stack grows to the centre

chapters.line: A shallow zinc skin, then Cr-Au and Sn-Pt-Sn contacts.
chapters.action: thin pink p+ skin appears at the top of layer 4; Cr-Au film on top (p side), Sn-Pt-Sn film under the substrate (n side); films uniform over the whole face, no stripe

chapters.line: A chip with no stripe; its bare end faces are the mirrors.
chapters.action: wafer slab narrows to one chip, plan drawn to scale (370 × 80), heights exaggerated; both end faces glint once; no cleaving animation (method not stated). Canvas label with the essential length and width

chapters.line: Flipped gold side down onto diamond on a copper block.
chapters.action: chip turns over (p side down) and lands on the Cr-Sn coated diamond, which sits on the copper block; the In-coated contact stand-in presses on the n side from above; drive stand-in leads to the In contact and to the Cr-Sn film on the diamond (assumed)

chapters.line: Light rises with dc current; pulsed drive shown for comparison.
chapters.action: model framed in the left half. The dc current is the plot pen x on the dc curve (0 to 0.854 A, where the drawn dc curve leaves the scale; last measured point 0.833 A; never beyond); end-face glow = min(L, L_B) / L_end (spontaneous, clamps at the bend); past the bend (about 0.81 A) a narrow beam = (L - L_B) / (L_end - L_B) along the 370 µm axis from both faces. Small heat arrows from layer 2 down through the diamond into the copper block. Pulsed curve drawn in the plot only (model shows dc). Prop leads fade

chapters.line: A broad glow sharpens into a laser line as current rises.
chapters.action: model holds the lasing state; the three Fig. 3 traces draw in order of current (0.1, 0.72, 0.80 A dc); hover gives the printed relative intensities I and peak energies

chapters.line: Lasing stays continuous with the copper block at 311 K.
chapters.action: final assembled state, beam on, no drive current (the paper gives only current densities at 311 K); canvas label on the copper block with the essential temperature; explode / orbit offered

Energy axis from the printed 10 meV bar, placed by the three printed peak energies (within about 1 meV); the paper draws energy increasing to the left. At 0.82 A the paper shows a single line no wider than 0.5 meV (3 Å) with I ≈ 100,000, beyond an apparent axis break: not plotted.

drawings.caption: US 3,758,875 FIG. 6A (Hayashi, Bell Labs)
drawings.note: Patent drawing: heat sink on the substrate side and a junction inside the narrow-gap region; the letter's diode was mounted p side down on diamond.
drawings.quote: The DH diode, shown in FIG. 6A with the dimensions exaggerated for the purposes of illustration, comprises in one embodiment a heat-sink 216 on which is formed a multilayered structure including a metal contact 219, a substrate 214, a wide band gap n-type layer 215, a narrow band gap region 224, a wide band gap p-type layer 212, a contact layer 217 and a second contact 218. It should be noted that it is readily possible to fabricate the heat sink on contact 218, or on both contacts 218 and 219.
drawings.remark: Same inventor and laboratory, filed 1970-05-01, before this letter. The patent's example grows the same four layers (n-AlGaAs with Sn, compensated p-GaAs with Si, p-AlGaAs with Zn, p-GaAs with Ge) on n-GaAs in a sliding holder (col. 8:14 to col. 9:35), but that wafer had other thicknesses and was tested without a heat sink. FIG. 6A draws the heat sink on the substrate side and a p-n homojunction 226 inside region 224; in this letter the gold (p) side is bonded to diamond, and layer 2 is p-type, the FIG. 6B case where the junction lies at the layer 1 / layer 2 interface (the letter does not say where the junction lies).
